doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Joe Henry persuades him to make The Way of the World
summary: Allison was reluctant after unsold CDs; Joe Henry wooed Audre by email.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Beautiful song. You recorded as recently as two years ago.
Well, I did an album for Joe Henry. He told me in Germany that he wanted to record me, and I played on a show with his band. We played it in Germany...
He kept asking you to...
You kept saying no. Mose would say “no,” he had a lot of CDs out there, and they weren’t selling... You said bad things about that.
He just didn’t want to do it.
You just felt it would be another CD that people would ignore or something like that?
Yes.
But Joe kept writing...
He kept writing to you. He was wooing my mother.
That seems to be a good strategy.
Yes. [LAUGHS] And I...
Yes.
But Joe is a good email writer...
I’m sure he is.
It was kind of fun corresponding with him. Also, I just thought... Joe is a good producer, and it would be a different approach.
Yeah, I heard he was a good producer.
He was going to let Joe set up everything. It was going to be the first time he let anyone produce, really.
He was always saying he was just setting up the sound...
So you just flew out there, and you did it in the studio in his house.
Yes.
Are the pieces on that record things you’d written over the ten years before you made it?
Most of the songs were written before.
Earlier. You didn’t write any for that except “My Brain.”
Yes.
You did write “The Way Of The World,” right?
I wrote another one... “How Does It Feel”?
No. It was... Oh my God, why can’t I think of it? “I Know You Didn’t Mean It.”
Oh, yeah. That one that I... That’s because that was not one of my favorites. “I Know You Didn’t Mean It.”
Yeah. “I Know You Didn’t Mean It.”
You 86'ed that one, I guess.
Yeah.
[LAUGHS] I wasn’t crazy about... He wasn’t really enthusiastic about doing that.
